title: Periodic XOR inverse transform uses the same key bytes and the same phase
summary: If y[i] = x[i] XOR key[i mod k], XOR keys with the same phase byte by byte again to restore x[i].
detail: If the intercepted sample starts at offset j from the original sequence, the first sample uses key[j mod k]. Merely knowing the key length cannot determine the phase of the interception point.
boundary: This conclusion is for a given byte transformation; status feedback or variable-length encoding will change the index relationship.
relevance: When reviewing explicit transformations of byte validators, avoid erroneously counting from the beginning of the key after taking a substring.
